newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent weaker Wednesday, based on market orders at 1017 EDT, dealers said.
Prices are expected to drift within their recent range as players await the USDA's montly supply and demand report, released Thursday at 0830 EDT.
There are no changes expected from the last report, however, since the USDA will rely on its March planted area estimate of 14.48 million acres, to forecast production.
USDA will issue its final planted area estimate on June 30. Industry sources expect the July supply and demand report to provide more accurate estimates for the U.S. crop.

Rain and cool temperatures in the eastern part of the U.S. cotton belt have slowed the development of the crop. Weather Services Corp noted slowe development in the Delta and in parts of Texas, but the crop is almost completely planted.
Tuesday, July cotton closed 0.40 cent higher at 72.52 cents per lb, traded from 72.70 to 72.25 cents. New crop December went out 0.22 cent firmer at 74.96 cents.
An estimated 10,000 lots changed hands on the day.
